label: Stag antler points increase yearly until about six years old
measurable_quantities: antler tine count by known age; age at which tine count plateaus
candidate_data: Long-term individual-based red deer studies (e.g. the Isle of Rum study) with known-age antler measurements.

label: Hinds swallow the afterbirth immediately after giving birth
measurable_quantities: proportion of deer births followed by placentophagy
candidate_data: Published observations of parturition behaviour in red deer and other cervids; comparative reviews of placentophagy in mammals.

label: Sick animals treat themselves, e.g. dogs eat grass to vomit
measurable_quantities: association between illness signs and grass eating in dogs; frequency of vomiting after grass eating
candidate_data: Veterinary surveys of grass eating in domestic dogs and the zoopharmacognosy literature on animal self-medication.

label: The trochilus cleans the crocodile's teeth
measurable_quantities: documented observations of birds feeding inside crocodile mouths
candidate_data: Field observations of Nile crocodile basking behaviour and associated birds; the Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Pigeons pair for life
measurable_quantities: pair-bond duration; rates of divorce and extra-pair paternity in Columbidae
candidate_data: Studies of pair-bond fidelity and extra-pair paternity in columbids; Birds of the World species accounts.

label: Heavy-bodied birds like quails and partridges build no nests
measurable_quantities: nest type (scrape versus built nest) versus body mass and flight ability
candidate_data: Nest-type compilations in Birds of the World with body mass and wing shape from AVONET.

label: Partridge hens feign lameness to lure intruders from the brood
measurable_quantities: occurrence of distraction (injury-feigning) displays in galliforms
candidate_data: Comparative reviews of distraction displays in birds and Birds of the World species accounts.

label: Web-footed birds all live near water
measurable_quantities: habitat association of species with webbed feet
candidate_data: Foot morphology and habitat data in AVONET and Birds of the World.

label: Swans sing chiefly as they approach death
measurable_quantities: vocalization rate of swans near death; occurrence of swans far out at sea
candidate_data: Swan vocalization recordings in xeno-canto and the Macaulay Library; Birds of the World species accounts.

label: The cuckoo lays a single egg in another bird's nest and does not hatch it
measurable_quantities: number of cuckoo eggs per host nest; host species parasitized
candidate_data: Brood-parasitism host records and nest-record schemes such as the BTO Nest Record Scheme.

label: Cuckoos lay in others' nests because of their own cowardice
measurable_quantities: nest-defence behaviour of cuckoos versus related non-parasitic species
candidate_data: None known that directly bears on motive; comparative studies of the evolution of brood parasitism.

label: A pair of eagles needs a large territory and drives other birds away
measurable_quantities: eagle home-range and territory size; nearest-neighbour distances between eagle nests
candidate_data: Raptor telemetry studies of home range and published nest-spacing data for eagles.

label: The sea-eagle makes its young stare at the sun and kills those that cannot
measurable_quantities: parental behaviour toward nestlings in relation to sun exposure; causes of nestling death
candidate_data: Nest-camera studies of white-tailed eagle and osprey parental behaviour.

label: The fishing-frog lures prey with filaments in front of its eyes
measurable_quantities: presence and use of the illicium as a lure; burial behaviour
candidate_data: FishBase species accounts for Lophius and studies of anglerfish luring behaviour.

label: The torpedo stuns its prey with a shock from its body
measurable_quantities: use of electric discharge in prey capture; discharge voltage
candidate_data: FishBase species accounts for Torpedo and electrophysiological studies of electric-organ discharge.

label: The male sheat-fish guards the spawn for forty to fifty days
measurable_quantities: sex of guarding parent; duration of paternal guarding in days
candidate_data: FishBase species account for Silurus aristotelis and published studies of its paternal care.

label: All fish are carnivorous except a few, and carnivorous fish wander most
measurable_quantities: proportion of fish species with animal-dominated diets; movement range versus trophic level
candidate_data: Diet and trophic-level data in FishBase, with movement and migration data from tagging studies.

label: Only the sepia uses its ink for concealment; octopus and squid ink from fear
measurable_quantities: contexts of ink release (anti-predator decoy, concealment, hunting) by taxon
candidate_data: Behavioural studies of inking in cephalopods and SeaLifeBase species accounts.

label: The octopus changes colour to match nearby stones
measurable_quantities: background-matching colour change during hunting and alarm
candidate_data: Studies of cephalopod camouflage and background matching; SeaLifeBase.

label: The octopus as a rule does not live beyond one year
measurable_quantities: octopus lifespan; post-spawning senescence and mortality
candidate_data: Age and growth studies of Octopus vulgaris and SeaLifeBase life-history data.

label: The argonaut uses its web as a sail and arms as oars
measurable_quantities: observed surface sailing behaviour in Argonauta
candidate_data: Behavioural observations of Argonauta in the wild and SeaLifeBase species accounts.

label: Spiders spin from the surface of the body, not from an excretion

candidate_data: Spider silk-gland anatomy and developmental studies in the arachnology literature.

label: On each trip a bee visits flowers of only one kind
measurable_quantities: flower constancy: proportion of single-species pollen loads per foraging trip
candidate_data: Pollen-load analyses and flower-constancy studies in honey bees.

label: Bees kill most of their kings to prevent the hive splitting
measurable_quantities: fate of supernumerary queens and queen cells; relation to swarming
candidate_data: Apicultural studies of queen-cell destruction, queen duels and swarming.

label: A bee that stings dies because it loses its gut with the sting
measurable_quantities: sting autotomy and post-sting survival of workers
candidate_data: Studies of sting autotomy and post-sting mortality in Apis mellifera.

label: Older bees work indoors, younger bees forage outside
measurable_quantities: age of workers performing in-hive tasks versus foraging; hairiness by worker age
candidate_data: Age-polyethism studies with marked honey bee workers.

label: Bees carry a stone as ballast in high wind
measurable_quantities: observations of bees carrying stones or grit in windy conditions
candidate_data: Studies of honey bee flight and foraging under wind.

label: Worker wasps all die in winter; only the mother-wasps overwinter
measurable_quantities: worker survival through winter; overwintering caste and site
candidate_data: Life-history studies of temperate social wasps documenting colony cycle and queen hibernation.

label: Lions attack humans when old and their teeth are diseased
measurable_quantities: age and dental condition of man-eating and livestock-raiding lions
candidate_data: Studies of man-eating lions examining skulls and teeth, and records of livestock depredation by lion age.

label: The elephant breathes through its trunk to cross water
measurable_quantities: observations of elephants crossing deep water using the trunk as a snorkel
candidate_data: Field observations of elephant swimming and Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Hens that beat a cock become cock-like, even growing spurs
measurable_quantities: incidence of male-like plumage, crowing and spurs in hens; association with dominance
candidate_data: Poultry science literature on spontaneous sex reversal and masculinization in hens.

label: Castrated cocks lose their crest colour, crowing and sexual drive
measurable_quantities: comb size and colour, crowing and mating behaviour in caponized versus intact cocks, by age at castration
candidate_data: Classic and modern capon studies in poultry science and endocrinology.

label: Boys castrated before puberty keep a high voice; eunuchs never go bald
measurable_quantities: voice pitch, body hair and baldness in men castrated before puberty
candidate_data: Historical studies of castrati and eunuchs and clinical data on androgen deficiency and androgenetic alopecia.

label: Stags castrated before growing horns never grow them
measurable_quantities: antler growth and casting after castration at different ages

measurable_quantities: co-occurrence of absent upper incisors and rumination across mammals

label: Many birds change plumage colour and song with the seasons
measurable_quantities: seasonal moult into different plumage colours; seasonal change in song
candidate_data: Moult and plumage descriptions in Birds of the World and song recordings in xeno-canto.

label: The redbreast and the redstart are one bird in two seasonal forms
measurable_quantities: species identity of the two forms; seasonal occurrence of each species
candidate_data: Taxonomy in the Open Tree of Life and GBIF occurrence records by month in Greece.

label: Ground birds dust-bathe; waterside birds water-bathe
measurable_quantities: occurrence of dust-bathing and water-bathing by taxon and habitat

label: Like begets like: the parent's characters determine the offspring's

label: Some ants fly and others do not

label: Within a class animals differ by degree; across classes their parts are only analogous

label: Homogeneous tissues exist for the sake of the heterogeneous organs
candidate_data: none known

label: Blood is the final nutriment and its quantity follows food intake

candidate_data: Physiological studies of blood volume and plasma composition under fasting and feeding in humans and laboratory animals.

label: Deer and roe blood has no fibres and never coagulates
measurable_quantities: clotting time and fibrinogen concentration in cervid blood
candidate_data: Veterinary haematology reference values for cervids, e.g. Species360 ZIMS physiological reference intervals.

label: Bloodless animals are more timorous, freezing and discharging excretions when frightened
measurable_quantities: frequency of freezing, ink or excretion discharge and colour change as fear responses

label: Bull's blood coagulates faster than any other animal's
measurable_quantities: clotting time of bovine blood compared with other species; fibrinogen concentration in cattle and pigs
candidate_data: Comparative veterinary coagulation studies and species haematology reference intervals.

label: Horned animals lacking upper front teeth have suet; others have lard
measurable_quantities: melting point and saturation of body fat in ruminants versus non-ruminants
candidate_data: Animal fat composition data in food-composition tables (e.g. USDA FoodData Central) and lipid chemistry literature.

label: Fat animals are less prolific
measurable_quantities: fertility or litter size in relation to body fat within species
candidate_data: Livestock reproduction studies relating body condition to fertility, and human epidemiology of obesity and fertility.

label: The lion's bones have almost no marrow
measurable_quantities: medullary cavity size and marrow content in lion long bones compared with other mammals
candidate_data: CT scans of carnivore skeletons in MorphoSource and comparative cortical-bone thickness studies.

label: The brain is the coldest part of the body and bloodless in its substance
measurable_quantities: brain temperature relative to other organs; cerebral blood flow and vascularity
candidate_data: Human and animal brain-temperature measurements and cerebral blood flow data in physiology literature.

label: The brain exists to cool the heat of the heart
measurable_quantities: contribution of the brain to cooling the blood or heart; brain metabolic heat production
candidate_data: Thermal physiology studies of brain heat production and selective brain cooling in mammals.

label: Every animal with blood has a brain; no bloodless animal has one
measurable_quantities: presence of a brain or cerebral ganglia across animal taxa
candidate_data: Comparative neuroanatomy in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase; invertebrate neuroanatomy literature.

label: The brain causes sleep by chilling the blood rising after food
measurable_quantities: role of the brain in initiating sleep; post-meal drowsiness and blood flow
candidate_data: Sleep neuroscience literature on brain sleep-regulating circuits and postprandial somnolence.

label: Man has the largest brain for his size, and men larger than women
measurable_quantities: brain mass relative to body mass across species; brain mass in men and women, absolute and relative to body size
candidate_data: Comparative brain and body mass compilations (e.g. published mammal and bird brain-size datasets), PanTHERIA body masses, and human neuroimaging cohorts such as the UK Biobank.

label: Only in man does the bregma solidify last
measurable_quantities: age at closure of the anterior fontanelle in humans and other mammals
candidate_data: Comparative cranial ontogeny studies and skull CT collections in MorphoSource.

label: Man has more skull sutures than any animal, males more than females
measurable_quantities: number of cranial sutures by species and by sex
candidate_data: Comparative cranial anatomy and skull CT collections in MorphoSource; Uberon for suture inventories.

label: Crustaceans and testaceans have their hard supporting part outside
measurable_quantities: presence of an exoskeleton or shell; heat retention by shells
candidate_data: Comparative invertebrate anatomy in the Animal Diversity Web and SeaLifeBase; thermal biology studies of shelled invertebrates.

label: Cuttlefish and squid have an internal shell; the octopus has none
measurable_quantities: presence of cuttlebone, gladius or internal shell remnant; mantle length
candidate_data: Cephalopod anatomy in SeaLifeBase, the Tree of Life Web Project and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: The belly wall is boneless in all animals
measurable_quantities: presence of bones (e.g. gastralia) in the abdominal wall across vertebrates
candidate_data: Comparative skeletal anatomy in Uberon, the Phenoscape Knowledgebase and MorphoSource specimens.

label: Males' bones are harder than females', carnivores' harder than herbivores'
measurable_quantities: bone mineral density or hardness by sex; bone mineral density in carnivores versus herbivores
candidate_data: Bone densitometry studies in mammals and comparative bone-material-property literature; EltonTraits for diet classification.

label: The lion's bones are so hard they give off sparks when struck
measurable_quantities: hardness of lion bone; whether bone produces sparks when struck
candidate_data: Bone material-property measurements; none specific to lions known.

label: The dolphin, being viviparous, has bones rather than fish-spines
measurable_quantities: skeletal tissue type in dolphins
candidate_data: Cetacean skeletal anatomy in MorphoSource and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Selachians have cartilage instead of fish-spine, for undulating movement
measurable_quantities: skeletal tissue type in chondrichthyans; swimming mode of chondrichthyans
candidate_data: FishBase for chondrichthyan taxonomy and swimming mode; Uberon and Phenoscape for skeletal tissue annotations.

label: Neither cartilage nor bone grows again once cut off
measurable_quantities: regrowth of amputated bone or cartilage across taxa
candidate_data: Regeneration literature on limb, fin and antler regrowth in vertebrates.

label: The brain is insensible and not the cause of sensation
measurable_quantities: pain response to touching brain tissue; effect of brain lesions on sensation
candidate_data: Neurosurgical observations of awake craniotomy and lesion studies in the clinical neuroscience literature.

label: Birds and scaly oviparous quadrupeds have no external ears
measurable_quantities: presence of an external ear (pinna) across taxa

label: The seal has no external ears, only auditory passages
measurable_quantities: presence of an external ear in seals and other mammals
candidate_data: Pinniped anatomy in the Animal Diversity Web; mammal trait compilations such as PanTHERIA for taxon coverage.

label: Some animals close the eye with the lower lid; birds blink with a membrane
measurable_quantities: which eyelid closes the eye; presence and use of a nictitating membrane
candidate_data: Comparative ocular anatomy literature on eyelids and nictitating membranes in birds, reptiles and mammals.

label: Birds of prey are sharp-sighted, ground fowl are not
measurable_quantities: visual acuity in raptors versus galliforms
candidate_data: Published comparative avian visual-acuity measurements; AVONET for ecological traits and lifestyle.

label: Fishes, insects and crustaceans have no eyelids
measurable_quantities: presence of eyelids; mobility of the eyes (e.g. stalked eyes)
candidate_data: Comparative eye anatomy in Uberon, FishBase and arthropod morphology literature.

label: All hairy animals have eyelashes; birds and scaly animals lack them, except the ostrich
measurable_quantities: presence of eyelashes across taxa
candidate_data: Comparative integument studies of eyelashes in mammals and birds; the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Only man has lashes on both eyelids; no quadruped has a lower eyelash
measurable_quantities: presence of lower-lid lashes across mammal species
candidate_data: Comparative mammalian eyelash measurements in the published literature; museum specimen photographs.

label: The elephant uses its nostril as a hand
measurable_quantities: use of the trunk in feeding, drinking and uprooting vegetation
candidate_data: Elephant behavioural ecology studies and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Elephants breathe through the raised trunk when crossing water
measurable_quantities: snorkelling with the trunk during swimming; time spent in water
candidate_data: Field observations of elephant swimming behaviour and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Birds that pronounce letters best have the broadest tongues
measurable_quantities: tongue breadth; capacity for vocal imitation of human speech
candidate_data: Comparative studies of vocal mimicry in parrots and other birds, with tongue morphology from museum specimens; AVONET for taxon coverage.

label: All birds communicate with their tongues, some seeming to teach one another
measurable_quantities: prevalence of vocal communication across bird species; occurrence of vocal learning from tutors
candidate_data: Song-learning and vocal-learning literature, xeno-canto recordings, and AVONET for taxon coverage.

label: Serpents and lizards have long forked tongues suited to taste
measurable_quantities: tongue length and degree of forking; role of the tongue in chemical sensing
candidate_data: Squamate tongue morphology and chemoreception studies; The Reptile Database for taxon coverage.

label: The crocodile moves its upper jaw and its tongue adheres to the lower
measurable_quantities: which jaw moves during feeding; attachment of the tongue to the floor of the mouth
candidate_data: Crocodilian skull and jaw-mechanics studies, MorphoSource skull scans and The Reptile Database.

label: Purple snails bore through shells with their tongue
measurable_quantities: drilling of prey shells by muricid gastropods
candidate_data: Predatory drill-hole studies in marine gastropods, SeaLifeBase and WoRMS for taxon coverage, and the Paleobiology Database for fossil drill holes.

label: Sharp interlocking teeth and tusks never occur together
measurable_quantities: co-occurrence of tusks and interlocking carnassial/sectorial dentition across mammal taxa
candidate_data: Comparative dental morphology in MorphoSource specimens and Phenoscape character matrices, with taxa placed on the Open Tree of Life.

label: Nature gives each weapon only, or most fully, to animals that can use it
candidate_data: none known

label: Weapons such as horns and spurs are confined to or larger in males
measurable_quantities: presence and size of horns, antlers, tusks and spurs in males versus females of each species
candidate_data: Sexual-dimorphism trait data in the Animal Diversity Web and the Amniote Life-History Database, with antler/horn presence by sex from bovid and cervid species accounts.

label: All fishes have saw-like teeth except the parrot-fish (Scarus)
measurable_quantities: tooth shape (sharp/conical versus flat/grinding or fused) across fish species
candidate_data: Dentition and diet fields in FishBase, plus fish skull scans in MorphoSource.

label: Hook-clawed birds have hooked beaks and eat no vegetable food
measurable_quantities: beak curvature; fraction of plant matter in diet
candidate_data: Beak measurements and trophic niche in AVONET, and diet composition in EltonTraits.

label: True horns occur only in viviparous animals
measurable_quantities: presence of horn-like head appendages and their use in combat across taxa
candidate_data: Anatomy and behaviour accounts in the Animal Diversity Web and head-appendage characters in Phenoscape.

label: Deer alone have solid horns and alone shed them
measurable_quantities: horn/antler structure (solid bone versus keratin sheath over bony core); annual shedding
candidate_data: Cranial-appendage descriptions for Cervidae, Bovidae, Antilocapridae and Giraffidae in the Animal Diversity Web and Phenoscape.

label: No horned animal has front teeth in the upper jaw
measurable_quantities: presence of upper incisors in horned versus hornless mammal species
candidate_data: Dental formulae in the Animal Diversity Web and dental characters in Phenoscape, mapped on the Open Tree of Life.

label: Animals without a lung have no neck
measurable_quantities: presence of a lung; presence of a neck (cervical region) across vertebrate taxa
candidate_data: Cervical-region and lung characters in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase.

label: Only hairy, lunged animals have an epiglottis
measurable_quantities: presence of an epiglottis across vertebrate classes
candidate_data: Laryngeal anatomy in Uberon and Phenoscape, and comparative anatomy specimens in MorphoSource.

label: Only animals with blood have viscera
measurable_quantities: presence of heart, liver/digestive gland, kidney-like organs in invertebrate taxa
candidate_data: Invertebrate organ anatomy in Uberon and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: The heart is the first part formed and at once contains blood
measurable_quantities: order of organ formation in vertebrate embryos; timing of first heartbeat and blood in the heart
candidate_data: Embryonic staging series and developmental-stage ontologies (e.g. Hamburger–Hamilton chick stages, ZFIN zebrafish stages).

label: The heart is the source of all sensation, pain and pleasure
measurable_quantities: site of sensory integration (heart versus brain) as shown by lesion or recording experiments

label: Only in man does the heart lie to the left of centre
measurable_quantities: lateral position of the heart in the thorax across mammals

label: Only the horse and a kind of ox have a bone in the heart

measurable_quantities: number of heart chambers versus body mass across vertebrates

label: Animals with a large heart are timid, with a small heart courageous
measurable_quantities: relative heart mass (heart mass / body mass); measures of fearfulness or flight response

label: Viviparous animals have large blood-rich lungs, oviparous ones small dry lungs
measurable_quantities: lung mass and vascularity relative to body mass; lung volume when inflated
candidate_data: Comparative lung morphometry in the respiratory physiology literature (Europe PMC); lung characters in Phenoscape.

label: Heart and liver, and only these, are found in every animal with blood
measurable_quantities: presence of heart, liver, spleen, kidneys, lung across vertebrate taxa

measurable_quantities: presence of a urinary bladder across birds, reptiles and fishes
candidate_data: Urinary-bladder characters in Uberon and Phenoscape across reptiles, birds and fishes.

label: Feathered and scaly animals have no kidneys, tortoises excepted
measurable_quantities: presence of kidneys across birds, reptiles and fishes

label: The right kidney always lies higher than the left
measurable_quantities: craniocaudal position of right versus left kidney by species

label: Viviparous animals with front teeth in both jaws have a single stomach
measurable_quantities: presence of upper incisors; number of stomach chambers

label: Horned animals have several stomachs because they lack upper front teeth
measurable_quantities: number of stomach chambers; presence of upper incisors; presence of horns

label: The parrot-fish alone among fishes ruminates
measurable_quantities: regurgitation and re-chewing of food in parrot-fishes
candidate_data: Feeding-biology accounts in FishBase and the literature on the pharyngeal mill of Scaridae.

measurable_quantities: presence of milk-clotting enzymes (chymosin activity) in the stomachs of young ruminants and hares

label: Vipers and selachians produce eggs internally and bear live young
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode (oviparity, ovoviviparity, viviparity) by species

label: All fishes have a gall-bladder, mostly attached to the intestine
measurable_quantities: presence and attachment site of the gall-bladder across fish species

label: Horse, mule, ass, deer and roe have no gall-bladder
